title: Launch lane stewardship: capacity escrow, ops-surge rota, and rollback runbook
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Goal: Define and operationalize a single playbook for stewarding high-impact launches that touch runtime, console, and API surfaces. This ticket synthesizes capacity escrow allocations, a rotating ops-surge roster (day/night), soft-freeze windows, and deterministic rollback criteria so we can reduce cross-team thrash and shorten time-to-safe-rollout for model and runtime changes.

Scope and deliverables:
- Capacity escrow model: a per-launch reserved GPU pool proposal (min/max sizing), pegged to feature tier and regional footprint, with rules for reclaiming unused escrow. Includes formulas for peak QPS->GPU units and burst hedges.
- Ops-surge rota: staffing schedule templates (primary, secondary, night-shift), on-call handover checklist, and run-rate expectations for first 72 hours.
- Soft-freeze lanes & deconfliction: rules for scheduling blocking vs non-blocking launches during shared windows, and an automated calendar flagging mechanism (Calendar-as-code entry).
- Smoke and fidelity checks: telemetry smoke test definitions (latency/QPS/error thresholds, quality regression gates tied to prompt sets), and dashboard runbook links.
- Rollback telegraph: deterministic rollback triggers (SLO breach + quality regression + escalation approval path) and fast-fallback model variants list.
- Communications templates: launch start/stop messages, incident templates, and stakeholder cadence for exec updates.

Why different: Instead of another abstract release calendar, this playbook focuses on the operational primitives we repeatedly lacked in prior launches: escrow sizing that maps directly to autoscaler behavior, a defined night-shift cutover plan, and explicit rollback telegraph signals that map into the Console incident workflow.

- Calendar-as-code repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/launch-calendars/pull/402
- PRD (internal): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1LaunchPlaybooksSPRING2026

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Playbook doc published and reviewed by runtime, infra, ops, and console leads.
- Capacity escrow sizing calculator prototype accepted by ENG (unit tests + sample projections).
- Ops-surge rota template tested in a dry-run (one-sprint rehearsal) with handover checklist completed.
- Calendar flagging automation merged to the calendar-as-code repo and demonstrates blocking flag for at least one upcoming launch window.
- Rollback triggers wired to Console incident playbooks and smoke tests create automated alerts during a controlled canary window.
updates: 2026-02-20 - Ticket created by Avery Chen. Initial scoping and stakeholder list added. Asked ENG to validate minimum escrow sizing assumptions.

2026-02-26 - Kickoff meeting with runtime, console, and SRE. Agreed on three escrow tiers (small/medium/large) and initial sizing heuristics based on 95th percentile token throughput. Action: ENG to prototype sizing calculator (ENG-87234).

2026-03-02 - Ops-surge rota draft shared. Ops prefers repeating 4-day on / 8-day off cycle for surge; night-shift slot identified for APAC windows. Action: PM to coordinate payroll & on-call comp with People Ops.

2026-03-04 - Calendar-as-code PR opened to add 'blocking-launch' flag and soft-freeze lanes. Waiting on automated test to ensure flag prevents double-booking. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/launch-calendars/pull/402

2026-03-07 - Telemetry smoke test thresholds proposed: 99th pct latency <= 300ms above baseline, error rate delta <= 0.5% absolute, quality-recall regression <= 2% on canonical prompt set. Shared with Research for sign-off.

2026-03-10 - Playbook draft reviewed in cross-functional review. Feedback: Console team requests explicit mappings from rollback telegraph to Console's incident severity and notification channels. Added as follow-up task. Next steps: formal dry-run scheduled for 2026-03-18.

rollout_phases: Phase 0 - Draft & alignment: collect sizing heuristics, define smoke tests (complete).
Phase 1 - Prototyping: escrow calculator + calendar flagging automation (in progress).
Phase 2 - Dry-run: simulate one launch with ops-surge rota and telemetry smoke tests (scheduled 2026-03-18).
Phase 3 - Launch: use playbook for an actual small/medium launch; gather telemetry and postmortem.
Phase 4 - Iterate: refine sizing heuristics, codify templates, add to launch conductor runbooks.
